description: Facing limper(s): isolate-raise / over-limp(call) / fold, by limper count + hero position. Iso ranges value-skewed; over-limp reserved for speculative hands in multiway. BB entries (M3, RES-G Slice B) are the check-or-iso option node: raise/check only, never fold — checking is free. Live-specific.

rationale_parts.lead: Against one limper from UTG+2, raise only premium hands and call along with the speculative ones.
points: Raise 99+, AJs+, KQs and AQo+ to 5bb: these dominate a limper's weak range and survive when a player behind wakes up with a real hand.
The whole table still acts behind you, so thin raises are asking for trouble — keep the raising range tight.

Medium pairs and suited connectors (22–88, ATs, KJs, QJs, JTs, T9s, 98s) over-limp (call the 1bb behind the limper) to see a cheap flop with several players in — hitting a set or a straight there wins a big pot for a small price.

rationale_parts.lead: Against one limper from the lojack, raise a slightly wider range than the early seats would, and call with small pairs and suited connectors.
points: Raise 88+, ATs+, KJs+, QJs, AJo+ and KQo to 5bb — fewer players left behind you means fewer chances someone is sitting on a monster.
Raising here isolates the limper: you aim to play the pot heads-up, in position, against a player who has already shown weakness by limping.
Small pairs and suited connectors (22–77, A5s, KTs, QTs, JTs and friends) over-limp instead — they want a cheap, multiway flop where a hidden set or straight gets paid off.

rationale_parts.lead: Against one limper in the hijack, raise strong hands to isolate the limper, and just call with small pairs and suited connectors.
points: Raise 77+, suited aces and Broadways (A9s+, KTs+, QTs+, JTs) and ATo+/KJo+ to 5bb — the goal is to isolate the limper (raise to get the pot heads-up) while you have position on them.
A limper's range is capped (limping in usually means no premium hand), so a value-leaning raise often wins outright and dominates them when called.

Small pairs (22–66) and suited connectors (54s–98s) over-limp — call the 1bb behind the limper — for a cheap multiway flop: hit a set or a straight and you win a big pot for the smallest possible price.

rationale_parts.lead: Against one limper in the cutoff, raise a wide value range to isolate the limper, and over-limp the small speculative hands.
points: Raise 66+, suited aces and Broadways, and ATo+/KJo+ — sized up to 5bb to punish the dead money the limper left in the pot.
Isolating (raising to get the pot heads-up) works especially well here: you'll have position for the whole hand against a capped, weak range.
Small pairs (22–55) and low suited connectors over-limp for a cheap multiway flop — their profit comes from hitting hidden monsters and getting paid (implied odds), not from winning raises.

rationale_parts.lead: In the small blind against one limper, raise only a value-heavy range and complete with the speculative hands — you'll be out of position all hand, so choose carefully.
points: Raise 66+, suited aces and Broadways, and ATo+/KJo+ to 5bb: strong hands still want a heads-up pot even when out of position.
With speculative hands, complete (call the extra half-blind) rather than fold — the discounted price makes chasing sets and straights worth it.
Being out of position (acting first every street) is a real handicap, so skip thin raises that build a pot you can't control.

rationale_parts.lead: On the button against one limper, raise your widest isolation range of any seat — guaranteed position makes almost every decent hand a raise.
points: Raise 55+, most suited hands down to 87s (A7s+, K9s+, Q9s+, J9s+, T9s, 98s), and A9o+/KJo+ to 5bb.
Acting last on every street lets you win pots your cards alone wouldn't — that's why the button isolates hands other seats would fold.
The tiny pairs and weakest suited hands still prefer to over-limp: a small multiway pot is where their hidden-monster payoff (implied odds) lives.

rationale_parts.lead: Against two limpers in the cutoff, tighten the raising range and size up — this pot is going multiway whether you like it or not.
points: Raise 88+, ATs+, KTs+, QJs and AJo+ to 6bb (4bb plus 1 per limper): with two callers likely, your raising hands must play well against several opponents.
Speculative pairs and connectors over-limp — a pot with three or more players is exactly where set-mining and drawing beat thin raising.

rationale_parts.lead: In the small blind against two limpers, raise only a tight value core and complete everything else that's playable.
points: Raise 88+, suited Broadways and AJo+ to 6bb — out of position against two callers, only genuinely strong hands want a big pot.
Complete (call the discounted half-blind) with the pairs, connectors and small suited aces: in a guaranteed-multiway pot, cheap set-mining and drawing beat bloating the pot from the worst seat.

rationale_parts.lead: On the button against two limpers, tighten up and size up: raise hands that play well multiway and over-limp the rest.
points: Raise 77+, ATs+, KTs+, QJs, AJo+ and A5s to 6bb — 4bb plus 1 per limper.
Even a raise often gets called in two places here, so the raising hands must hold up against several opponents, not just one.
Speculative pairs and connectors over-limp: pots with three or more players reward hitting sets and straights more than thin isolation.

rationale_parts.lead: In the big blind against one limper you never fold — checking is free — so the only question is which hands raise.
points: Raise a wide value-plus-equity range (55+, suited aces and Broadways, T9s/98s, ATo+/KJo+) to 5bb: punish the limper's dead money and thin the field.
Everything else checks and takes the free flop — the big blind's range is weaker overall, and building a pot out of position with a marginal hand helps your opponent, not you.

rationale_parts.lead: In the big blind against two limpers, raise a tighter value core and check everything else — the free flop is yours either way.
points: Raise 77+, suited aces and Broadways, and AJo+/KQo to 6bb (4bb plus 1 per limper): a raise here still gets called somewhere, so the raising hands must play well multiway.
Every other hand checks its option — a free look at the flop with a speculative hand beats folding, and beats building a pot you'd have to play out of position.

rationale_parts.lead: Against three limpers in the big blind, raise only the premium top for pure value and check everything else.
points: Raise 99+, AJs+, KQs and AQo+ to 7bb (4bb plus 1 per limper): with three callers in, bluffs and thin raises have nowhere to go — this raise is for value only.
Every other hand — including the medium pairs and suited connectors that love a cheap four-way flop — checks the free option.
